description: Pythium species are soilborne pathogens that cause damping-off and root rot in many crops. The disease mainly attacks seedlings, causing soft watery rot near the soil line that leads to plant collapse and death.
symptoms: Irregular patches of wilted or yellow plants in seedbeds
Soft brown watery rot at the base of stems
Seedlings falling over at the soil line
Yellowing of older plants due to root damage
Stem rot in newly transplanted plants
visual_symptoms: patches of dead or stunted seedlings
favorable_conditions: Dense seedbeds with poor air circulation
spread: Contaminated tools or trays in nurseries
disease_cycle: Pythium survives in soil as spores or mycelium
Spores germinate in wet soil conditions
Pathogen infects seeds or young seedlings
Infected tissues produce more spores that spread through water
impact: Yield reduction due to weak plant stands
cultural_control: Use sterile soil or seedling substrate
biological_control: Use beneficial fungi such as Trichoderma species
Use beneficial bacteria like Bacillus subtilis
chemical_control: Seed treatment with fungicides such as metalaxyl or mefenoxam
Soil drenches with appropriate fungicides in nurseries
source: Plant pathology references on Pythium damping-off
